page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16-lssd is an ARM64-based server powered by 16 dedicated physical cores of the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor family running at 3.0 GHz. It features 64.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core, and includes 1608 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU architecture operates with 1.0 thread per physical core and does not support hyperthreading. Cache specifications include 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 80 MB L3 cache. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results show top-tier memory performance, with the Passmark memory score placing in the top 10% of tested servers. Large-block read-only and write-only memory bandwidth benchmarks are strong, registering in the top 25% at 314.24 GB/sec and 120.6 GB/sec respectively. Computational performance is average for single-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests, but multi-core Geekbench scaling is strong. Text processing, gzip compression, and bzip3 decompression also perform in the top 25%. Database operations under Passmark are strong, while Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput remain in the average tier.

The server offers qualitative cost efficiency by bundling high-capacity local NVMe SSD storage with dedicated ARM cores, reducing the need for external storage attachments for disk-heavy workloads. However, the ARM64 architecture lacks x86-specific vector and matrix extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX, which limits its suitability for certain legacy workloads or specialized x86 instruction sets. Given its high-speed local storage, strong memory performance, and solid multi-core scaling, this server is suited for database operations, text processing, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and general-purpose containerized workloads.
